slot.brief: Ask which transition metal ion is colourless in aqueous solution and why (d0 or d10 configuration), with coloured d-partly-filled ions as distractors.

stem: Which aqueous ion is colourless because its electronic configuration permits no $d$–$d$ transition?

verdicts.working: Sc³⁺ has a 3d⁰ configuration, so it has no d electrons and cannot undergo a d–d transition. The other ions have partially filled d orbitals.

working:
$\text{Sc}^{3+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^0$; no $d$ electrons, so no $d$–$d$ transition is possible.
$\text{Ti}^{3+}$, $\text{V}^{3+}$ and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ have partially filled $d$ subshells and can undergo $d$–$d$ transitions.

Independent check: Sc³⁺ has a 3d⁰ configuration, so it has no d electrons and cannot undergo a d–d transition. The other ions have partially filled d orbitals.
solution: A $d$–$d$ transition requires electrons in partially filled $d$ orbitals. For $\text{Sc}^{3+}$, the configuration is $[\text{Ar}]3d^0$, so no $d$–$d$ transition is possible. Thus, $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ is colourless.
